_README: Code-table knob for the tbl_use_case integer columns. Editing this file changes what the
assistant says; no code change is needed. Same seam as config/rule_text_semantics.json.
WHY PROVENANCE IS A FIELD HERE, not a comment:
business_category has THREE sources and they do not agree, so 'is this code legal' has three
different answers depending on who you ask:
1. the DATA DICTIONARY (owner-relayed screenshot, 2026-08-05) defines 0-7 and stops there;
2. BusinessCategoryEnum.java on the mirror additionally defines 8, 10-21, 32, 34, 35;
3. the real UAT rows additionally CONTAIN 33 (1 row, B0001) and 37 (6 rows, I0135-I0140),
all with status=Y, i.e. active.
Flattening those into one 'known enum' is what produced the earlier claim that 33/37 were
'unregistered new categories'. They are not: nothing defines them anywhere. Codes 8-35, by
contrast, ARE defined — just not in the dictionary excerpt we were shown, which is a weaker
statement and must not be reported as drift.
So each entry carries the source that defines it, and only a code defined by NEITHER source is
a data-contract defect. A code in `code_enum` but not `data_dictionary` is reported as such and
is NOT an alarm — the dictionary excerpt may simply be older or narrower than the code.
The table these columns belong to is inferred from the neighbouring columns in the same
screenshot (bounce_back periods, mi_category, has_order_status, send_mode) which match
tbl_use_case. If that inference is ever contradicted, fix it here rather than in code.
Adding a code: put it under the source that actually defines it. Never move a code into
`data_dictionary` to silence a warning.

business_category._source: data dictionary screenshot relayed by the project owner, 2026-08-05

code_enum._source: BusinessCategoryEnum.java on the mirror — defined in code, absent from the dictionary excerpt above

_note: An INDEPENDENT third statement of the send semantics that tbl_use_case_ext.rule_text and
tbl_use_case_channel_rule.priority both also describe. The three map onto each other:
send_mode 3 (single channel)<-> rule_text no operator, or '|' (exclusive_choice)
That mapping is used ONLY to CROSS-CHECK rule_text, never to override it: rule_text stays
authoritative per the 2026-07-27 owner answer. A disagreement is reported as a data-quality
finding, exactly like the existing rule_text-vs-priority disagreement.
_measured_2026_08_05: CONFIRMED PRESENT in the real UAT master export (the column bound successfully), so the
optimistic binding paid off. Observed distribution:
code 3 -> 1,435 rows      send by single channel
code 0 ->   903 rows      *** STILL UNEXPLAINED — and the second most common value ***
code 2 ->   249 rows      send by priority
code 1 ->   148 rows      send at the same time
code 5 ->    72 rows      mixed mode        (supplied 2026-08-06)
code 4 ->     3 rows      send by separately (supplied 2026-08-06)
2026-08-06: the full dictionary page arrived and closed 4 and 5. The first excerpt had been
cut off after 3, which is why they looked undefined. Code 0 remains genuinely unexplained.
Note what 5 unlocked: 'Mixed mode' is the dictionary's own name for what rule_text calls
MIXED, so a mixed expression can now be checked POSITIVELY instead of being skipped as
uncomparable. Code 4 gets NO rule_text_equivalent on purpose — the expression grammar has no
operator for 'separately', and mapping it to the nearest-looking one would manufacture
agreement or disagreement out of nothing.
The cross-check found 30 rule_text disagreements on the real export. OPEN owner question:
expected historic drift, or a data-quality exception? Until answered they are reported at
warning severity with rule_text named as the winner, which is the safe reading.
KEEP IN SYNC with SEND_MODE_ENUM / SEND_MODE_RULE_TEXT_EQUIVALENT / SEND_MODE_PENDING_MEANING
in retriever/usecase_catalog.py — a test asserts they match, because this file WINS when
present and a code added only to the seed would silently do nothing.

_README: Codes seen in the real data whose meaning has not been supplied. This is a THIRD state,
deliberately not merged with 'undefined': code 0 covers ~903 rows, so it is plainly a
legitimate and widely used value that we simply cannot read yet. Calling that
data-contract drift overstates the problem; saying nothing understates it. Rows carrying a
pending code are excluded from the cross-check and reported at INFO, not WARNING.
Move a code from here into `data_dictionary` the moment the owner explains it.
pending_meaning.0: appears on ~903 rows of the real UAT export — a legitimate, widely used value whose meaning the data dictionary does not give. Owner question outstanding since 2026-08-06. Rows carrying it are excluded from the rule_text cross-check; their send semantics rest on rule_text alone, which is authoritative anyway.
